nv_hot_tub_club.blurb: Hot Tub Club is a small bouldering zone on the east side of Kraft Boulders, in the Calico Basin corner of Red Rock outside Las Vegas. Fifteen sandstone problems cluster around one big block, with a spread that runs from V2 up to V8: a few in the V3 and V4 range, a solid group at V6, and a handful of hard lines above that. That makes it better suited to people already climbing V5 and up than to beginners. The trail leads past The Pearl and just before Alexisizer, and the block sits beside the east end of Bill's Boulder. Topping out the easiest line means a tricky downclimb or a jump, so scout it first.

nv_circus_cliff.blurb: Circus Cliff is a short sandstone wall in the Calico Hills of Red Rock, reached in a few minutes from the First Pullout lot on the scenic loop. It holds fifteen climbs, a mix of bolted sport lines and trad routes with a few top-rope options. Most grades fall between 5.10 and 5.12, with a small number of easier pitches, so it suits climbers working through the 5.10s and 5.11s more than novices. The wall catches sun from late morning into the afternoon and is somewhat sheltered from weather. Being so close to the parking area, it is popular, and you can hear and see the lot from the base.

nv_turtle_shell.blurb: Turtle Shell is a single large sandstone boulder sitting up on a hillside in the Main Cluster of the Red Spring Boulders, in Calico Basin near Las Vegas. Problems start on every side, and a few roof and cave lines come out of the east face. The fifteen problems stretch from V1 to V9, with a cluster of moderates around V3 and a strong group of hard lines from V7 to V8, including some of the area's best-known test pieces. Look for the biggest block toward the southeast end of the cluster. The surrounding Red Spring zone gets shade in the afternoon as the sun drops behind the hill.

nv_case_face_the.blurb: The Case Face is a sandstone cliff in the Willow Spring area of Red Rock, an easy walk from the Ragged Edges buttress next door. Of its fifteen routes, thirteen are trad and two are sport, covering grades from about 5.4 up to 5.10, with the bulk in the 5.6 to 5.9 range. Several are multi-pitch, so it works well as a quieter moderate day for a pair comfortable placing gear; protection is a mix of cams and fixed pieces. Willow Spring in general offers short approaches and some shaded climbing through much of the year, which makes it a good early-season choice, though it fills up on fine weekends.

nv_seraphim_wall.blurb: Seraphim Wall is a recessed stretch of the Angel Food Wall in Red Rock, lying between Purblind Pillar and Lean Lady and facing east-northeast. All fifteen routes are trad, mostly in the 5.7 to 5.9 range with a big cluster at 5.8, so it is a good objective for climbers stepping up to longer moderate lines. Cracks tend to fade out partway up the face, which keeps most routes to one to four pitches, and a few continue to the top. The sandstone is generally excellent. Expect a steep hillside approach through thick brush, finishing with a wandering fourth-class scramble.

nv_lower_east_side.blurb: The Lower East Side is a large buttress low on the east flank of Mt. Wilson, the highest peak in Red Rock Canyon. It offers fifteen trad routes, all moderate: nearly all sit at 5.8 or 5.9, with one 5.7. Climbing here was sparse until the 2000s, so it has a quieter, more remote feel than the roadside crags. The walk in follows a faint old jeep track from the First Creek trailhead, crossing washes and entering a small canyon before a ridge leads to the base. Plan on two rappels for the way down, the first short and the second long enough to need a double rope.
